notable_facts: Consensus sits at the TOP of company guidance at both levels: Q2 EPS $0.25 vs a $0.15-0.25 guide, and FY27 $2.24 vs a $2.15-2.25 guide. No cushion.
Q3 FY27 consensus of $1.71 is ~76% of the full-year $2.24. Q3 FY26 delivered $1.90 non-GAAP of a $2.61 year (73%). The October quarter is the entire thesis.
FY27 guidance explicitly excludes Marc Jacobs, a ~$500m acquisition expected to close in fiscal Q3 2027 and expected to be dilutive for the first 12 months.
The FY26 buyback ($49.8m) has been switched off for all of FY27 to fund the deal - zero shares repurchased in Q1 FY27 despite a fresh 10m-share authorisation.

Unremediated material weakness (ITGCs at the KLH/Karl Lagerfeld subsidiary, ~9% of FY26 sales) with an ADVERSE Ernst & Young opinion on internal control as of 2026-01-31; CEO and CFO concluded disclosure controls were NOT effective in the Q1 FY27 10-Q.

A judgemental $140m IEEPA tariff receivable sits in prepaid expenses ($191.5m at 2026-04-30 vs $53.0m at 2026-01-31); Q1 FY27 operating cash flow was -$2.0m vs +$93.8m a year earlier despite $1.50 of GAAP EPS.
Customer concentration: Macy's 20.6%, TJX 11.4%, Ross 11.0% of FY26 net sales; top ten 67.6%. Roughly 43% of revenue through three accounts, two of them off-price.
Calvin Klein + Tommy Hilfiger were 28.0% of FY26 sales (34.0% in FY25); licences expire on a staggered basis to 2027-12-31; FY27 loses ~$470m of sales.

Zero open-market insider buys or sells by any officer or director in calendar 2026 - all Form 4 activity is grants and tax withholding. The CEO's three-year price/relative-TSR PSU vested at MAXIMUM (840,000 shares on a 700,000 target, +20% TSR modifier) on 2026-08-18, two weeks before the print.
Short interest at a two-year high in absolute shares (7.59m, +25% since 2026-05-29), 20.98% of float, 18.6 days to cover.

20-day realised vol is 20.5% - the 0.6th percentile of the last two years. The stock has been unusually quiet into the print, then broke a ten-session range with -2.60% on 1.96x average volume on 2026-08-31.

Peer regime is violently bifurcated: DTC specialty beat and rallied (ANF +35.7% on 2026-08-26, URBN +9.5%, GAP +12.9% on 08-28) while every wholesale-dependent brand owner de-rated (TPR -20.7%, CPRI -19.1%, CRI -18.8%, PVH -16.5%, LEVI -15.7%) and the customer base fell (BURL -29.5%, TJX -15.0%, M -15.4%, KSS -11.3%). GIII's -10.5% month is cohort beta.

The tape is punishing guidance, not results: Tapestry beat both lines and fell 16.5% on FY27 guidance; TJX raised the full year and fell on a two-cent Q3 miss; Burlington beat EPS by 35% and fell 7.6% on revenue.

Tariff regime changed twice since guidance was set: IEEPA struck down 2026-02-20, replaced by Section 122 (+10pp flat), which expired 2026-07-23 and was replaced 2026-07-24 by two-tier Section 301 forced-labour tariffs (10% for Bangladesh/Cambodia/Indonesia/Malaysia, 12.5% for Vietnam). MY INFERENCE: this is neutral-to-modestly-favourable versus the June assumption of 'rates that existed under the IEEPA tariff regime', which weakens the most obvious bear case and is the main reason the direction score is moderate rather than strongly negative.
PVH reports the same day, after the close on 2026-09-02 - simultaneously G-III's largest expiring licensor and the company taking those categories in-house.
